html:
A Mandinka trader turned soldier who built the Wassoulou Empire in the upper Niger region from the 1860s and fought the French from 1882 to 1898.

He took the title almami and ruled from Bissandugu near Kankan, with an army armed with repeating rifles, some made by his own smiths. Pressed by French columns, he moved his whole state east into what is now Ivory Coast and Ghana, destroying the old city of Kong on the way. The French captured him in 1898 and he died in exile in Gabon in 1900. Sekou Toure claimed descent from him, and in Guinea he is a national hero of resistance to French rule.
